gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-noto-serif-kr: Bruno Ace SC strings its wide-open letters along like beads, with crossbars as fat as the stems they join. Noto Serif KR, a classic serif, is gentler, with mild thick-thin shifts.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-noto-serif-sc: Noto Serif SC is rounded and a little literary. Its strokes thicken gently at the sides, while Bruno Ace SC looks laser-cut from one unvarying stroke width, so a long passage moves from crisp mechanical lettering into softer, tapered rhythm.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-noto-serif-tc: Refined and traditional, Noto Serif TC holds its letters open with stems barely heavier than their arms, set against the wire-like tubes of Bruno Ace SC. One is made for striking display lettering; the other for quiet steady text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-petrona: Bruno Ace SC draws every letter with a single constant stroke, spread wide and open for display. And Petrona, a classic serif, brings moderate thick-thin transitions that feel dignified and editorial beneath it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-poly: Bruno Ace SC keeps even its joins slim as pipe cleaners. Poly, a bookish text serif, adds a restrained stem-to-connector difference, and that mix of technical heading and literary body is the pair's greatest strength.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-quattrocento: Rounded bowls with no swelling at all give Bruno Ace SC its engineered, spread-out look in display sizes. Quattrocento, a serif with modest contrast like lightly engraved brass lettering, does the quieter job of carrying text with daylight inside every curve.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-radley: Curves without any stress give Bruno Ace SC a smooth, spread-out, machined feel at the top. Radley, a classic serif drawn as if with a barely tilted nib, lets the eye slip in and out of its counters across a full page.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-roboto-serif: Dignified and classic, with big open eyes on every e and a, Roboto Serif spaces its letters generously. Bruno Ace SC, with its hairline-free, swell-free forms, makes the pair's strongest quality a clear split between display bluntness and low-contrast serif text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-sahitya: Technical-pen steadiness meets bookish warmth here: Bruno Ace SC spreads its open letters wide, while Sahitya, a classic serif, keeps its thin strokes clearly thinner yet never fragile. Over many paragraphs, Sahitya stays uncrowded and traditional.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-sawarabi-mincho: Refined is the mood: Bruno Ace SC bends its lines like rope or tubing, with open apertures throughout. Sawarabi Mincho, a classic serif with terminals cut short and stems a touch heavier than the crossbars, would read steadily and traditionally through a long passage.
